question: Does 100! (100 factorial) end in exactly 24 zeros?

claims.text: Each trailing zero comes from a factor of 10 = 2×5, so the zero count is the smaller of the exponents of 2 and 5.
Factors of 2 are far more plentiful than factors of 5, so the count of 5s determines the number of zeros.
There are 20 multiples of 5 up to 100.
There are 4 multiples of 25 up to 100, each contributing an extra factor of 5.
There are no multiples of 125 up to 100.
The total exponent of 5 in 100! is 24.
The exponent of 2 in 100! is 97, which exceeds 24.
A common error is stopping at 20 by forgetting the extra 5s from 25, 50, 75, and 100.
The answer of 20 zeros (or any value other than 24) is ruled out.
